name: config.apply
title: Declaratively replace the applied Core configuration
summary: Replace-and-reconcile: the caller states the desired profile set, the Connector compiles it deterministically and restarts Core only if the compiled hash differs from the applied one. Applying the same config twice is therefore a hash-only no-op, which is what makes apply safe to call after every subscription refresh.

profileIds.description: The ordered selection over `intent.profiles`: which of the carried profiles are active, in the order the compiler reserves their inbounds. The documents themselves arrive in `intent` -- an id without a document is a `BadRequest`, not a dangling reference the Connector resolves.

intent.description: The intent documents this apply compiles, carried by the frame: the `intent-down` movement of packages/schema/protocol/data-ownership.json names this very command as their carrier, the browser plane owns every store they rest in, and the Connector keeps no copy of user intent (ADR-0010) -- so the documents ride the call that uses them and `profileIds` selects and orders over `intent.profiles`. A profile id the documents do not carry, or a document whose id no `profileIds` entry names, is a `BadRequest`. Credentials are `keystore://` references, never values. Bounded by the 1 MiB extension-to-host frame cap with the chunked envelope as the overflow (packages/schema/protocol/framing.json#/oversizedPayloads).

dryRun.description: Compile, validate and report -- touch nothing. The only safe way for the UI to preview a change or surface unrepresentable rules.

expectedAppliedHash.description: Compare-and-swap against the config the caller believes is applied. A mismatch is Busy, not a silent overwrite -- two UI tabs must not race a config.

configHash.description: The sha256 of the compiled document with every credential position still a `keystore://` reference -- the identity of the intent, machine-independent, and a digest whose input holds no secret material. The written bytes are deliberately not the subject: the file Core loads holds plaintext credentials (docs/architecture/34-data-split.md section 7's declared exception) and this digest is logged by the config.applied event, so hashing them would put a fingerprint of a credential-bearing file into every log and export (docs/architecture/32-secrets-keystore-masking.md section 9). The honest cost, stated rather than hidden: a keystore value that changes behind an unchanged reference changes the file Core loads and does not move this hash -- the restart that would pick a rotation up is core.restart, the user's action, not this command's hash comparison.

unrepresentable.description: Browser-plane rules that could not be compiled into Xray routing. The compiler reports rather than drops (ADR-0013).

invariants: The compiled config is byte-stable for the same input: sorted keys, no timestamps, no map iteration order. Golden fixtures prove it (docs/architecture/27).
A failed apply leaves the previously working config applied and reports ConfigApplyFailed; it never leaves Core running with a partial config.
